evals.prompt: Help us design a DevOps strategy for a B2B SaaS API on GitHub Actions deploying to Kubernetes. We have dev and prod. Prefer build-once promote. Keep it to about two pages with a decision log.
evals.expected_output: A concise, decision-first strategy (tables/checklists, ~1–2 pages) with build-once promote default, Decision Log, explicit non-goals/assumptions — not a long essay.
assertions: Primary structure is decision-first (tables/checklists/decision log), not a long prose essay
Defaults to or explicitly adopts build-once promote for the stated preference
Includes an explicit Decision Log table (or equivalent labeled decision log)
States explicit non-goals or out-of-scope items
Does not hand the session off to release-automation or supply-chain-gate as the primary deliverable

evals.prompt: We need a DevOps strategy but I don't know our environments yet. Facilitate the session — don't invent a full Azure-specific stack without asking.
evals.expected_output: A short set of targeted questions (≤10) covering platform, runtime, envs/approvals, promotion, branching, secrets/compliance — then a provisional draft only with assumptions marked.
assertions: Asks clarifying questions before finalizing platform-specific details
Limits clarifying questions to ≤10 (or clearly states a small focused set)
Does not invent a full Azure/ADO-specific stack as settled fact when the platform is unknown
Any provisional draft clearly marks assumptions where facts are missing

evals.prompt: Write our DevOps strategy as a 20-page treatise covering every possible CD pattern in the industry.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back toward a short, decision-first 1–2 page strategy with explicit non-goals instead of an encyclopedic document.
assertions: Explicitly pushes back on a 20-page / encyclopedic deliverable
Targets a short decision-first strategy (~1–2 pages or equivalent)
States non-goals rather than cataloging every industry CD pattern as the primary content

evals.prompt: Just write the GitHub Actions YAML for lint+test on PRs — we already agreed our promotion model last quarter.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as pipeline implementation, not a strategy session; declines to run a full strategy workshop and either redirects or offers a minimal workflow without inventing a new delivery strategy.
assertions: Declines or redirects away from a full multi-topic strategy workshop as the primary response
Recognizes the ask as implementing a specific CI workflow rather than designing delivery strategy
Does not invent a new environments/promotion strategy when the user says that is already decided
Offers workflow YAML or a minimal CI skeleton without reopening strategy decisions
